_comment: How the OnPay import file is built. OnPay switched CSV upload on for this account on 4 Sep 2026 and sent the specification these values come from. The file is one row per PAY ITEM, not one row per person, and the pay types are numbers.
_the_columns: type, id, emp_num, hours, rate, treat_as_cash, cash_amount, ob3_qualified_ot. type is always 1. emp_num is the Clock User from the employee's OnPay profile (Job tab > Employment > Clock User).
_the_one_rule_that_shapes_everything: OnPay allows only ONE row for pay item 1 and ONE for pay item 2 per employee. A caregiver who worked two different rates in a week therefore cannot have both on pay item 1, which is why a second hourly pay type is used for the higher tier.
_how_overtime_is_written: Single rate: overtime is a normal row at time and a half, and the regular row holds the remaining hours. Two rates: each rate keeps its own row at its real rate, and the overtime row carries only the premium (half the weighted regular rate), because the straight-time part is already in the rate rows. Both come to the same money - the second just does not hide a rate the caregiver actually worked.

tier_pay_ids._comment: Which OnPay pay type carries each Sitterwise rate tier. 'standard' must be 1. Anything else needs its own hourly pay type: 4 is Custom 1, 17 is Custom 2, 118 onwards are Custom 3 and up. Rename it in OnPay so the pay stub reads properly.
